The best chain on garnet is QB11-QB12-QB7. QB12 sits in the middle. I took the numbers from the current default calibration set, f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade. That set has IRB CZ fidelities for all 28 CZ pairs. The pair QB11-QB12 has a CZ fidelity of 0.998693. The pair QB12-QB7 has 0.998016. Their product is 0.996712, which is the highest of any connected 3-qubit chain. The next best chain is QB12-QB11-QB16, with a product of 0.994689.

I ran a 3-qubit GHZ circuit on exactly those three physical qubits on garnet:mock with 200 shots. The job ID is 01a1603f-b266-727b-84bb-d218a2b5e8cd. It completed. The circuit puts QB12 into an equal mix of 0 and 1 with a native rotation. It then copies QB12 onto QB11 and onto QB7. Each copy step uses one CZ gate between two single-qubit rotations. The CZ gates act only on QB11-QB12 and QB12-QB7. Then all three qubits are measured, in the order QB11, QB12, QB7.

The counts were 000: 56, 011: 46, 100: 51, 111: 47. A real GHZ state gives only 000 and 111, about half each. That is because the three qubits are entangled and always agree. These counts do not show that, and this is expected. The mock backend returns random placeholder counts that do not depend on the circuit. The mock run checks that the server accepts the circuit on these qubits and gates. It does not show entanglement. A run on the real garnet would show mostly 000 and 111. You would see a few other results because each gate has a small error. Picking the chain with the highest CZ fidelities keeps those errors as low as the chip allows. This run cost no credits.
